subject: math
title: Grade 2 Equality and Inequality (=, ≠, <, >)
seo_title: Grade 2 Equality and Inequality Worksheets (=, ≠, <, >): Free Math with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Symbolic representation of equality and inequality
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on equality and inequality for the BC curriculum: balances with = and ≠, comparing numbers to 100 with < and >, true or false number sentences, missing numbers and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: = means “is the same as”. ≠ means “is not equal to”. The open side of < and > faces the bigger number.
key_sub: 4 + 4 ≠ 6 + 3, because 8 is not 9. 42 > 37, because 4 tens is more than 3 tens. In 6 + 7 = 10 + □, the box is 3, not 13.
body_html:
= means “is the same as”. ≠ means “is not equal to”

Think of a balance. When both sides are the same, it is level. Write =. When they are not the same, the heavier side goes down. Write ≠.

SentenceLeft sideRight sideSign
9 + 6 and 151515=
8 + 5 and 121312≠
7 + 7 and 10 + 41414=

< and >: the open side faces the bigger number

< means “is less than”. > means “is greater than”. Read from left to right. Look at the tens first. If the tens are the same, look at the ones.

Example

Which sign goes in the box? 8 + 7 □ 14

Work out each side first. 8 + 7 = 15. 15 is greater than 14.

Answer: 8 + 7 > 14

Find the missing number

A box □ stands for a number we do not know. Work out the side you know. Then find what makes the other side the same.

Example

40 = 25 + □

Count on from 25 to 40: 25 to 30 is 5, 30 to 40 is 10. 5 + 10 = 15. Check: 25 + 15 = 40.

Answer: 15

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
42 < 37 (< and > mixed up)The open side faces the bigger number: 42 > 37
37 is bigger than 42, because 7 > 2Look at the tens first: 4 tens > 3 tens
6 + 4 = 10 + 2 (= means “the answer is”)Both sides must be the same. 10 is not 12, so 6 + 4 ≠ 10 + 2
6 + 7 = 10 + □, so □ = 1313 is the left side. 10 + □ = 13, so □ = 3
40 = 25 + □, so □ = 25 (smaller digit from larger)Count on: 25 to 30 is 5, 30 to 40 is 10. □ = 15

faq.q: What does equality and inequality mean in Grade 2 math?
faq.a: Equality means two amounts are the same, written with =. Inequality means they are not the same, written with ≠, or with < and > to show which one is less or greater.

faq.q: How can my child remember which way < and > go?
faq.a: The open side always faces the bigger number. In 42 > 37 it opens toward 42, and in 37 < 42 it still opens toward 42.

faq.q: Where is equality in the BC Grade 2 math curriculum?
faq.a: It is in Patterning: “symbolic representation of equality and inequality.” Students show equal and not equal with balances and pictures and write number sentences with = and ≠, using numbers to 100.
Many children read = as “the answer is”. Show a balance: both sides must be the same, so 6 + 7 = 10 + 3.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the balance?
items.e: The left side has 6 + 4 = 10. The right side has 10. The balance is level, so 6 + 4 = 10.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the balance?
items.e: The left side has 7 + 5 = 12. The right side has 9. 12 is not 9, and the balance is not level, so 7 + 5 ≠ 9.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the balance?
items.e: The left side has 8. The right side has 3 + 5 = 8. The balance is level, so 8 = 3 + 5.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the balance?
items.e: The left side has 4 + 4 = 8. The right side has 6 + 3 = 9. 8 is not 9, and the heavier side goes down, so 4 + 4 ≠ 6 + 3.

items.q:
Which sign goes in the box? Why?
9 + 6 □ 15
items.e: 9 + 6 = 15. The right side is 15 too. Both sides are the same, so use =: 9 + 6 = 15.

items.q:
Which sign goes in the box? Why?
8 + 5 □ 12

Which sign goes in the box? Why?
10 □ 4 + 6
items.e: 4 + 6 = 10. Both sides are 10, so use =: 10 = 4 + 6. The answer does not have to go last.

items.q:
Which sign goes in the box? Why?
7 + 7 □ 10 + 4
items.e: 7 + 7 = 14 and 10 + 4 = 14. Both sides are 14, so use =: 7 + 7 = 10 + 4.

items.q:
Which sign goes in the box? Why?
20 + 30 □ 60
items.e: 2 tens + 3 tens = 5 tens, so 20 + 30 = 50. 50 is not 60, so use ≠: 20 + 30 ≠ 60.

items.q:
Which sign goes in the box? Why?
15 − 5 □ 5 + 5
items.e: 15 − 5 = 10 and 5 + 5 = 10. Both sides are 10, so use =: 15 − 5 = 5 + 5. The signs + and − can be different.

items.q: Which number sentence is true?
items.e: 5 + 3 = 8. 8 is not 7, so 5 + 3 ≠ 7 is true. 5 + 3 ≠ 8 is false, because both sides are 8.

items.q: Work out each side. Which one is true?
items.e: 6 + 6 = 12. Both sides are 12, so 12 = 6 + 6 is true. 6 + 7 is 13, not 12.

items.q: Which one is true? Check both sides.
items.e: 40 + 10 = 50. 50 is not 40, so 40 + 10 ≠ 40 is true. 40 + 10 ≠ 50 is false, because both sides are 50.

items.q: Which number sentence is false?
items.e: 9 + 9 = 18, not 19. So 9 + 9 = 19 is false. It should be 9 + 9 ≠ 19.

items.q: Work out each side. Which one is false?
items.e: 10 + 20 = 30. Both sides are 30, so 30 ≠ 10 + 20 is false. It should be 30 = 10 + 20.

items.q: Which one is false? Check both sides.
items.e: 16 − 8 = 8, not 9. So 16 − 8 = 9 is false.

items.q: What does the ≠ sign mean?
items.e: ≠ means is not equal to. The two sides are not the same. 5 + 2 ≠ 8, because 7 is not 8.

items.q: What does the = sign mean?
items.e: = means is the same as. In 6 + 4 = 5 + 5, both sides are 10. The answer does not always come next.

items.q: Kai writes 6 + 4 = 10 + 2. Is he right?
items.e: 6 + 4 = 10, but 10 + 2 = 12. 10 is not 12, so the sentence should be 6 + 4 ≠ 10 + 2. Kai read = as “the answer is”.

items.q: Zara writes 3 + 5 ≠ 5 + 3. Is she right?
c: Yes. The order is not the same.
items.e: 3 + 5 = 8 and 5 + 3 = 8. Both sides are the same, so it should be 3 + 5 = 5 + 3. Changing the order does not change the total.

items.q: The signs < and > have an open side. Which number does the open side face?
items.e: The open side always faces the bigger number. In 9 > 4, it faces 9. In 4 < 9, it faces 9 too.

items.q: What does 35 > 28 mean?
items.e: Read from left to right. > means “is greater than”. So 35 > 28 means 35 is greater than 28. The open side faces 35.

items.q: What does 19 < 40 mean?
items.e: Read from left to right. < means “is less than”. So 19 < 40 means 19 is less than 40. The open side faces 40.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 42 has 4 tens. 37 has 3 tens. 4 tens is more, so 42 is greater. The open side faces 42: 42 > 37. Look at the tens first, not the ones.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 25 has 2 tens. 52 has 5 tens. 5 tens is more, so 52 is greater. The open side faces 52: 25 < 52. Look at the tens first, not the ones.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 63 has 6 tens. 36 has 3 tens. 6 tens is more, so 63 is greater. The open side faces 63: 63 > 36. Look at the tens first, not the ones.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Both have 5 tens. Look at the ones: 54 has 4 and 59 has 9. So 59 is greater. The open side faces 59: 54 < 59.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 30 has 3 tens. 27 has 2 tens. 3 tens is more, so 30 is greater. The open side faces 30: 30 > 27. Look at the tens first, not the ones.

items.q:
Which sign goes in the box? Why?
8 + 7 □ 14
items.e: 8 + 7 = 15. 15 is greater than 14. The open side faces 15: 8 + 7 > 14.

items.q:
Which sign goes in the box? Why?
56 □ 65
items.e: 56 has 5 tens. 65 has 6 tens. So 56 is less than 65. The open side faces 65: 56 < 65.

items.q:
Which sign goes in the box? Why?
30 + 40 □ 70
items.e: 3 tens + 4 tens = 7 tens, so 30 + 40 = 70. Both sides are 70: 30 + 40 = 70.

items.q:
Which sign goes in the box? Why?
50 − 20 □ 20 + 20
items.e: 50 − 20 = 30 and 20 + 20 = 40. 30 is less than 40. The open side faces 40: 50 − 20 < 20 + 20.

items.q:
Which sign goes in the box? Why?
9 + 9 □ 20 − 1
items.e: 9 + 9 = 18 and 20 − 1 = 19. 18 is less than 19. The open side faces 19: 9 + 9 < 20 − 1.

items.q: Which one is true? Look at the signs.
items.e: 48 has 4 tens and 84 has 8 tens, so 48 < 84. The others face the wrong way: 57 < 75, 62 > 26, 39 < 93.

items.q: Which one is true? Work out the sum first.
items.e: 60 + 6 = 66. Both sides are 66, so 66 = 60 + 6. 6 + 6 is only 12.

items.q:
Which number makes this true?
□ > 58
items.e: □ > 58 means the box is greater than 58. 61 has 6 tens, so 61 > 58. Not 58: 58 is equal to 58, not greater. Not 49: 4 tens is less than 5 tens.

items.q:
Which number makes this true?
27 < □
items.e: 27 < □ means the box is greater than 27. 30 is greater than 27. Not 18: look at the tens first. 1 ten is less than 2 tens.

items.q:
Which number makes this true?
□ < 40
items.e: □ < 40 means the box is less than 40. 38 has 3 tens, so it is less than 40. Not 40: 40 is equal to 40, not less.

items.q: Ryan writes 23 < 19. Is he right?
items.e: Look at the tens first. 23 has 2 tens and 19 has 1 ten, so 23 is greater: 23 > 19. Ryan looked at the ones.

items.q: Leah writes 15 + 5 > 20. Is she right?
items.e: 15 + 5 = 20. Both sides are 20, so the right sign is =: 15 + 5 = 20.

items.q:
True or false?
9 + 4 = 13
items.e: 9 + 4 = 13. Both sides are 13. So 9 + 4 = 13 is true.

items.q:
True or false?
15 = 8 + 7
items.e: 8 + 7 = 15. Both sides are 15. So 15 = 8 + 7 is true.

items.q:
True or false?
6 + 6 ≠ 12
items.e: 6 + 6 = 12. Both sides are 12. So 6 + 6 ≠ 12 is false.

items.q:
True or false?
7 + 5 ≠ 11

True or false?
24 > 42
c: True. 4 ones is more than 2 ones.
items.e: 24 is less than 42. So 24 > 42 is false.

items.q:
True or false?
36 < 63
c: False. 6 ones is more than 3 ones.
items.e: 36 is less than 63. So 36 < 63 is true.

items.q:
True or false?
8 + 8 > 15
items.e: 8 + 8 = 16. 16 is greater than 15. So 8 + 8 > 15 is true.

items.q:
True or false?
10 + 3 < 12
items.e: 10 + 3 = 13. 13 is greater than 12. So 10 + 3 < 12 is false.

items.q:
True or false?
20 + 20 = 30 + 10

True or false?
14 − 7 < 8
items.e: 14 − 7 = 7. 7 is less than 8. So 14 − 7 < 8 is true.

items.q:
True or false?
50 + 5 ≠ 55
items.e: 50 + 5 = 55. Both sides are 55. So 50 + 5 ≠ 55 is false.

items.q:
True or false?
45 > 40 + 6
items.e: 40 + 6 = 46. 45 is less than 46. So 45 > 40 + 6 is false.

items.q:
True or false?
30 − 10 = 10 + 10
c: False. One is − and one is +.

items.q:
True or false?
17 + 3 < 30
items.e: 17 + 3 = 20. 20 is less than 30. So 17 + 3 < 30 is true.

items.q:
True or false?
60 > 59
c: False. 9 ones is more than 0 ones.
items.e: 60 is greater than 59. So 60 > 59 is true.

items.q:
True or false?
40 + 30 = 80 − 10
c: False. One is + and one is −.

items.q:
True or false?
25 + 25 > 50
items.e: 25 + 25 = 50. Both sides are 50. So 25 + 25 > 50 is false.

items.q:
True or false?
72 − 2 ≠ 70
items.e: 72 − 2 = 70. Both sides are 70. So 72 − 2 ≠ 70 is false.

items.q: Which number sentence is true? Find the sum first.
items.e: 35 + 5 = 40. 40 is greater than 39, so 35 + 5 > 39 is true. 35 + 5 ≠ 40 is false, because both sides are 40.

items.q: Which number sentence is false? Find the sums first.
items.e: 9 + 9 = 18. Both sides are 18, so 18 < 9 + 9 is false. 9 + 8 = 17, and 18 is greater than 17, so the other three are true.

items.q:
The balance is level.
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The box is the same as 8 + 5. 8 + 5 = 13. Not 3: that subtracts.

items.q:
The balance is level.
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The box is the same as 16 − 7. 16 − 7 = 9. Not 23: that adds. Not 11: you cannot take 7 from 6, so regroup a ten.

items.q:
The balance is level.
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The left side is 6 + 7 = 13. So 10 + □ must be 13 too. 13 − 10 = 3. Not 13: that is the left side, not the box. = does not mean “the answer is”.

items.q:
The balance is level.
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The left side is 9 + 6 = 15. So □ + 5 = 15. 15 − 5 = 10. Not 15: that is the left side. Not 20: that adds 15 and 5.

items.q:
The balance is level.
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The left side is 20 + 30 = 50. So 40 + □ = 50. 50 − 40 = 10. Not 50: that is the left side. Not 90: that adds 50 and 40.

items.q:
The balance is level.
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The left side is 15 + 10 = 25. So □ + 20 = 25. 25 − 20 = 5. Not 25: that is the left side. Not 15: 20 is more than 10, so the box must be less than 15.

items.q:
□ + 8 = 14
What number goes in the box?
items.e: What adds to 8 to make 14? 14 − 8 = 6. Check: 6 + 8 = 14. Not 22: that adds.

items.q:
9 + □ = 17
What number goes in the box?
items.e: Count on from 9 to 17: 1 to make 10, then 7 more. 1 + 7 = 8. Check: 9 + 8 = 17. Not 26: that adds. Not 12: that takes the smaller digit from the larger.

items.q:
40 = 25 + □
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The = sign can come first. 25 + □ = 40. Count on: 25 to 30 is 5, 30 to 40 is 10. 5 + 10 = 15. Not 65: that adds. Not 25: that takes the smaller digit from the larger.

items.q:
12 + 4 = □ + 6
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The left side is 12 + 4 = 16. So □ + 6 = 16. 16 − 6 = 10. Not 16: that is the left side. Not 14: 6 is 2 more than 4, so the box must be 2 less than 12, not 2 more.

items.q:
30 + 15 = 35 + □
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The left side is 30 + 15 = 45. So 35 + □ = 45. 45 − 35 = 10. Not 45: that is the left side. Not 20: 35 is more than 30, so the box must be less than 15.

items.q:
□ + 25 = 20 + 30
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The right side is 20 + 30 = 50. So □ + 25 = 50. 50 − 25 = 25. Not 50: that is the right side. Not 75: that adds 50 and 25.

items.q:
18 − 8 = 15 − □
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The left side is 18 − 8 = 10. So 15 − □ = 10. 15 − 10 = 5. Not 10: that is the left side. Not 11: 15 is less than 18, so take away less than 8.

items.q:
50 − 20 = 40 − □
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The left side is 50 − 20 = 30. So 40 − □ = 30. 40 − 30 = 10. Not 30: that is the left side. Not 70: that adds 40 and 30.

items.q:
45 + 5 = 60 − □
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The left side is 45 + 5 = 50. So 60 − □ = 50. 60 − 50 = 10. Not 50: that is the left side. Not 110: that adds 60 and 50.

items.q:
70 = □ + 36
What number goes in the box?
items.e: □ + 36 = 70. Count on: 36 to 40 is 4, 40 to 70 is 30. 4 + 30 = 34. Not 106: that adds. Not 46: that takes the smaller digit from the larger.

items.q:
63 − □ = 40
What number goes in the box?
items.e: 63 take away what leaves 40? 63 − 40 = 23. Check: 63 − 23 = 40. Not 103: that adds. Not 40: 40 is what is left, not what was taken away.

items.q:
□ − 15 = 47
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The box is the number you start with. Undo − 15 by adding: 47 + 15 = 62. 7 + 5 = 12, so regroup a ten. Check: 62 − 15 = 47. Not 32: that subtracts. Not 52: that forgets the regrouped ten.

items.q:
25 + 25 = 30 + □
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The left side is 25 + 25 = 50. So 30 + □ = 50. 50 − 30 = 20. Not 50: that is the left side. Not 30: 30 is 5 more than 25, so the box must be 5 less than 25.

items.q:
100 = 58 + □
What number goes in the box?
items.e: 58 + □ = 100. Count on: 58 to 60 is 2, 60 to 100 is 40. 2 + 40 = 42. Not 158: that adds. Not 52: from 60 to 100 is 4 tens, not 5 tens.

sets.title: Word problems: equal or not equal

items.q: Liam has 34 hockey cards. Ava has 43 hockey cards. Which is true?
items.e: 34 has 3 tens. 43 has 4 tens. So Liam has fewer cards: 34 < 43. The open side faces 43.

items.q: At the beach, Mei finds 18 shells. Owen finds 9 shells in the morning and 9 in the afternoon. Which is true?
items.e: Owen finds 9 + 9 = 18 shells. Mei finds 18. They are the same: 18 = 9 + 9.

items.q: A BC Ferries boat has 46 cars on the top deck and 64 cars on the lower deck. Which deck has more cars?
items.e: 64 has 6 tens. 46 has 4 tens. So 64 > 46. The lower deck has more cars.

items.q: On Monday, the class sees 52 salmon in the river. On Tuesday, they see 25 salmon. Which is true?
items.e: 52 has 5 tens. 25 has 2 tens. More salmon on Monday: 52 > 25. The open side faces 52.

items.q: Chloe has 15 stickers. She gets some more. Now she has 24. How many stickers did she get?
items.e: 15 + □ = 24. Count on: 15 to 20 is 5, 20 to 24 is 4. 5 + 4 = 9. Not 39: that adds. Not 11: that takes the smaller digit from the larger.

items.q: Arjun reads 8 books in March and 6 books in April. Nadia reads 15 books. Which is true?
items.e: Arjun reads 8 + 6 = 14 books. 14 is not 15: 8 + 6 ≠ 15.

items.q: A whale-watching boat sees 12 orcas in the morning and 9 orcas in the afternoon. Another boat sees 20 orcas. Which boat sees more orcas?
items.e: The first boat sees 12 + 9 = 21 orcas. 21 > 20, so the first boat sees more. Add both times before you compare.

items.q: Hana has 3 dimes and 1 nickel. A freezie costs 40¢. Does she have enough money?
items.e: 3 dimes are 30¢. 1 nickel is 5¢. 30¢ + 5¢ = 35¢. 35¢ < 40¢, so she does not have enough. Count the value, not the number of coins.

items.q: Ethan has 20 red blocks and 6 blue blocks. Sofia has 16 blocks. How many more blocks does Sofia need to have the same number as Ethan?
items.e: 20 + 6 = 16 + □. Ethan has 20 + 6 = 26. So 16 + □ = 26, and the box is 10. Not 26: that is Ethan’s total. Not 42: that adds 26 and 16.

items.q: A Grade 2 class runs laps for the Terry Fox Run. The goal is 50 laps. They have run 35 laps. How many more laps do they need?
items.e: 35 + □ = 50. Count on: 35 to 40 is 5, 40 to 50 is 10. 5 + 10 = 15. Not 85: that adds. Not 25: that takes the smaller digit from the larger.

items.q: A SkyTrain car has 48 people. At a station, some people get off. Now 30 people are on the car. How many got off?
items.e: 48 − □ = 30. 48 − 30 = 18. Check: 48 − 18 = 30. Not 78: that adds. Not 30: 30 is how many are left.

items.q: In one year, Nanaimo has 20 rainy days in November and 5 rainy days in July. How many more rainy days are in November?
items.e: 5 + □ = 20. Count on from 5 to 20, or 20 − 5 = 15 days. Not 25: that adds.

items.q: Simran picks 27 apples at an orchard in Kelowna. She wants 40 apples. Which number sentence shows how many more she needs?
items.e: She starts with 27, picks some more (the box) and ends with 40: 27 + □ = 40. The box is 13.

items.q: Jasleen has more than 45 beads and fewer than 50 beads. How many beads could she have?
items.e: The number must be > 45 and < 50. 47 works: 47 > 45 and 47 < 50. Not 45 or 50: they are equal, not more or fewer. Not 54: 54 > 50.

items.q: Kai skis down Grouse Mountain 12 times on Saturday and 9 times on Sunday. Leah skis down 22 times. Who skis down more times?
items.e: Kai skis 12 + 9 = 21 times. 22 > 21, so Leah skis more times. Not Kai: 21 is less than 22.

items.q: Wei counts 9 bald eagles in a tree and 8 on the riverbank. Lucas counts 18 bald eagles. Which is true?
items.e: Wei counts 9 + 8 = 17 eagles. 17 is less than 18. The open side faces 18: 9 + 8 < 18.

items.q: The soccer team has 14 players. 9 players are on the field. The rest are on the bench. How many are on the bench?
A ferry has room for 60 bikes. 38 bikes are on the ferry. How many more bikes can get on?
items.e: 38 + □ = 60. Count on: 38 to 40 is 2, 40 to 60 is 20. 2 + 20 = 22. Not 98: that adds. Not 38: that takes the smaller digit from the larger.

items.q: Owen has 30 red beads and 15 blue beads. Ji-woo has 40 beads. How many more beads does Ji-woo need to have the same number as Owen?
items.e: 30 + 15 = 40 + □. Owen has 30 + 15 = 45. So 40 + □ = 45, and the box is 5. Not 45: that is Owen’s total. Not 25: 40 is more than 30, so Ji-woo needs fewer than 15.

items.q: Sofia has 50¢. She buys a pencil for 35¢. Ava has 20¢. Who has more money now?
items.e: Sofia has 50¢ − 35¢ = 15¢ left. 20¢ > 15¢, so Ava has more. Not 25¢: from 35¢ to 50¢ is 15¢. Not 50¢: Sofia spent some of it. 15¢ > 20¢ faces the wrong way.
